Undermanned side upsets finals-bound ACT Brumbies 21-19 Players come together to mark victory and club’s expected demise An undermanned Moana Pasifika have capped off their potential final match with a stirring victory, upsetting the finals-bound ACT Brumbies 21-19. But there were mixed feelings as players celebrated a rare win before coming together with staff to mark the occasion of the club’s farewell game and expected demise with an emotionally charged hymn. The Super Rugby Pacific club was placed into liquidation on Monday after their current owners announced that they would not continue to fund the franchise beyond 2026 on April 15. Unless a last-minute saviour comes in to salvage the club, only introduced in 2022, they will fold and the competition will shrink to 10 teams in 2027.

But Pasifika (2-12) relished the occasion at GIO Stadium on Saturday and snapped a 12-game losing streak to avoid a record-equalling 13th loss. The cellar dwellers’ victory wasn’t smooth sailing though, as the Brumbies led both on the scoreboard and numerically when barnstorming inside centre Faletoi Peni was handed a second yellow card and sent off in the second half. But the hosts couldn’t make the most of their opportunity and substitute Melani Matavao stormed over in the 73rd minute to claim victory. This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.

The tactic first hit the mainstream with Erasmus’s Springboks last summer, showcasing the approach first in their victorious Test series against Italy and then reprising it in a thrilling defeat to Australia at Ellis Park at the beginning of last year’s Rugby Championship. South Africa’s attempts did eventually lead to two tries in a 45-0 victory over the Azzurri but neither was as effective as Moana Pasifika’s. The Springboks did not redeploy the tactic on their autumn tour of the northern hemisphere.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Undermanned side upsets finals-bound ACT Brumbies 21-19

Players come together to mark victory and club’s expected demise

An undermanned Moana Pasifika have capped off their potential final match with a stirring victory, upsetting the finals-bound ACT Brumbies 21-19.

But there were mixed feelings as players celebrated a rare win before coming together with staff to mark the occasion of the club’s farewell game and expected demise with an emotionally charged hymn.

The Super Rugby Pacific club was placed into liquidation on Monday after their current owners announced that they would not continue to fund the franchise beyond 2026 on April 15.

Unless a last-minute saviour comes in to salvage the club, only introduced in 2022, they will fold and the competition will shrink to 10 teams in 2027.

But Pasifika (2-12) relished the occasion at GIO Stadium on Saturday and snapped a 12-game losing streak to avoid a record-equalling 13th loss.

The cellar dwellers’ victory wasn’t smooth sailing though, as the Brumbies led both on the scoreboard and numerically when barnstorming inside centre Faletoi Peni was handed a second yellow card and sent off in the second half.

But the hosts couldn’t make the most of their opportunity and substitute Melani Matavao stormed over in the 73rd minute to claim victory.

This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.

“With all that had happened during the week, in terms of Moana going into liquidation, we [knew we wouldn’t] see a lot of our group that we left behind,” Umaga said.

“We talked a lot about our strong purpose of who we represent. We’re representing our culture, our people, and we saw that come through in the end.

“[In all] the emotion of the last few months, today, I couldn’t tell you what happened in those other games ... I can tell you what happened today, and I’m very proud of it. This one stands out.”

The Brumbies (7-7) needed a big bonus-point win to help them move as high as fourth on the ladder, but instead will have to settle for sixth.

Their faltering lineout and a series of errors will be a concern for coach Stephen Larkham and the Brumbies now face the table-topping Hurricanes across the Tasman and must win to secure a berth in a qualifying final.

Moana Pasifika have perfected one of Rassie Erasmus’s pioneering tactics, with the Super Rugby Pacific franchise scoring a try from an open-play line-out lift in defeat by the Blues on Saturday.The Auckland-based side, which is set to be disbanded at the end of the season owing to financial struggles, scored from the unusual scenario in the first half of a 45-19 defeat to the Blues at Auckland’s Go Media Stadium.Mills Sanerivi, Moana Pasifika’s hooker, scored the first of his two tries off the back of the move, during which Alex Craig, the former Gloucester lock, was lifted into the air by his two props one pass after a tapped penalty.Craig and his fellow home forwards then manufactured a maul which the Blues tried to collapse, to no avail. Sanerivi crashed over and received a joyous reception from his team-mates and replacements. Head coach Tana Umaga, the former All Black centre, and defence coach Alando Soakai could not hide their delight from the television cameras, either.

The tactic first hit the mainstream with Erasmus’s Springboks last summer, showcasing the approach first in their victorious Test series against Italy and then reprising it in a thrilling defeat to Australia at Ellis Park at the beginning of last year’s Rugby Championship. South Africa’s attempts did eventually lead to two tries in a 45-0 victory over the Azzurri but neither was as effective as Moana Pasifika’s. The Springboks did not redeploy the tactic on their autumn tour of the northern hemisphere.

Erasmus revealed last July that the Springboks had in fact copied the tactic from a schoolboy side in South Africa. “We actually saw it done by a school side, Paul Roos Gymnasium, where Willie [Le Roux] was. With the maul in open play, you get all the benefits like in a line-out maul when you support the player jumping.

“It worked twice for us [leading to tries], but people saw it, so it will be done [stopped] for the next couple of games.”

payload.title: Moana Pasifika päätti kautensa tunteikkaaseen voittoon Brumbiesista
payload.summary: Moana Pasifika voitti ACT Brumbiesin 21–19 Super Rugby Pacificin ottelussa, joka saattoi jäädä seuran viimeiseksi. Joukkue päätti illan yhteiseen virteen seuran epävarman tulevaisuuden keskellä.
payload.content:
Moana Pasifika päätti mahdollisesti viimeiseksi jäävän Super Rugby Pacific -ottelunsa yllättävään 21–19-voittoon ACT Brumbiesista lauantaina GIO Stadiumilla. Vajaamiehinen joukkue katkaisi samalla 12 ottelun tappioputkensa ja juhli voittoa tilanteessa, jossa seuran tulevaisuus näyttää erittäin epävarmalta.

## Voitto vaikeasta asemasta

Moana Pasifika lähti otteluun altavastaajana. ACT Brumbies oli matkalla pudotuspeleihin, kun taas Pasifika oli sarjan häntäpäässä saldolla 2–12. Ottelun merkitys kasvoi urheilullista tulosta suuremmaksi, sillä seuran odotetaan katoavan sarjasta, ellei uutta rahoittajaa löydy.

Voitto ei tullut helposti. Brumbies johti ottelua sekä pistetaululla että pelaajamäärässä, kun sisäkeskushyökkääjä Faletoi Peni sai toisen keltaisen korttinsa ja joutui ulos toisella puoliajalla. Kotijoukkue ei kuitenkaan kyennyt hyödyntämään ylivoimaansa ratkaisevasti.

Ratkaisu nähtiin 73. minuutilla, kun vaihtopelaaja Melani Matavao murtautui maalialueelle ja vei Pasifikan johtoon. Osuma riitti kääntämään ottelun vieraille ja estämään sen, että joukkue olisi päättänyt kautensa ennätystä sivuavaan 13. peräkkäiseen tappioon.

## Seuran tulevaisuus vaakalaudalla

Ottelun jälkeen tunnelma oli ristiriitainen. Pelaajat juhlivat harvinaista voittoa, mutta kokoontuivat samalla henkilökunnan kanssa merkitsemään hetkeä, jota pidetään mahdollisena jäähyväisenä. Tilaisuus päättyi tunteikkaaseen yhteiseen virteen.

Moana Pasifika asetettiin selvitystilaan maanantaina. Nykyiset omistajat olivat ilmoittaneet 15. huhtikuuta, etteivät he jatka seuran rahoittamista vuoden 2026 jälkeen. Jos viime hetken pelastajaa ei löydy, vuonna 2022 sarjaan liittynyt seura lopettaa toimintansa ja Super Rugby Pacific supistuu vuonna 2027 kymmeneen joukkueeseen.

## Päätös vaikealle kaudelle

Lauantain voitto antoi joukkueelle ainakin urheilullisesti arvokkaan päätöksen vaikealle kaudelle. Se syntyi tilanteessa, jossa joukkue oli vajaamiehinen, vastustaja oli pudotuspeleihin etenevä Brumbies ja seuran oma tulevaisuus oli avoin. Samalla yhteinen virsi korosti, että kyse ei ollut vain yksittäisestä ottelutuloksesta, vaan myös mahdollisesta päätöshetkestä seuralle, pelaajille ja taustajoukoille.
summary_bullets: Moana Pasifika voitti ACT Brumbiesin 21–19 mahdollisesti viimeisessä Super Rugby Pacific -ottelussaan.
Joukkue katkaisi 12 ottelun tappioputken ja ratkaisi ottelun 73. minuutilla Melani Matavaon yrityksellä.
Seura on selvitystilassa, ja ilman uutta rahoittajaa sen odotetaan lopettavan toimintansa vuoden 2026 jälkeen.

The Super Rugby Pacific club was placed into liquidation on Monday after their current owners announced that they would not continue to fund the franchise beyond 2026 on April 15. Unless a last-minute saviour comes in to salvage the club, only introduced in 2022, they will fold and the competition will shrink to 10 teams in 2027.

But Pasifika (2-12) relished the occasion at GIO Stadium on Saturday and snapped a 12-game losing streak to avoid a record-equalling 13th loss. The cellar dwellers’ victory wasn’t smooth sailing though, as the Brumbies led both on the scoreboard and numerically when barnstorming inside centre Faletoi Peni was handed a second yellow card and sent off in the second half.
